title: Section H – AOD Parenting Capacity Assessment
focus: Observable parenting capacity and child safety while using alcohol or other drugs.

groups.title: Substance Use Assessment
items: Recent use and current level of impairment.
History of overdose, blackouts, or severe intoxication.
Impact of substance use on daily functioning.

groups.title: Child Safety Assessment
items: Are basic needs met? (food, hygiene, supervision, medical care, education).
Has the child ever been left unsupervised?
Has the child been exposed to dangerous situations?
Is there access to hazardous substances, needles, or medications?

groups.title: Home Environment Assessment
items: Cleanliness and physical safety of the home.
Availability of food and basic necessities.
Presence of domestic violence or high conflict.
Other adults in the home and their influence.

groups.title: Protective Factors
items: Supportive family members or social network.
Engagement with treatment or recovery supports.
Insight into substance-related risks to children.

groups.title: Risk Indicators
items: Frequent intoxication while caring for children.
Driving under the influence with children present.
History of neglect or prior child protection involvement.
Child injuries related to supervision failures.
Refusal of treatment despite ongoing impairment.
Very young children requiring constant supervision.

groups.title: Assessment Conclusion
guidance: Base conclusions on observable evidence, not assumptions about substance use alone.
Consider current level of impairment, parenting functioning, and impact on child safety.
Weigh protective factors alongside risk indicators.
Determine overall risk level (e.g., low, moderate, high) and required response.
